title: Protocol for Generating a 3D Culture of Epiblast Stem Cells
author: Rosa, Sato, et al.

steps.title: Thaw and plate mESCs
steps.instruction: Warm a frozen mESC vial at 37 °C, coat a well of a 12‑well plate with 1 mL 0.1 % gelatin, add the thawed cells to 10 mL pre‑warmed mESC base medium in a 15 mL Falcon tube, centrifuge 200 × g for 5 min, aspirate the gelatin from the plate and the supernatant from the tube, resuspend the pellet in 1 mL mESC medium (base + 2iLif) and plate onto the gelatin‑coated well at an ideal density of 2 × 10⁴ cells / cm², then incubate.

steps.title: Maintain mESC culture
steps.instruction: Replace the medium the next day with 1 mL fresh mESC medium and thereafter change medium every 2 days until colonies reach the appropriate confluence for passaging.

steps.title: Passage mESCs
steps.instruction: Pre‑warm mESC base medium, mESC medium and 0.05 % trypsin‑EDTA at 20 °C for 10–20 min, coat a 12‑well well with 1 mL 0.1 % gelatin, remove medium, wash with 1 mL PBS, add 500 µL trypsin‑EDTA, incubate 37 °C for 5 min, inactivate trypsin by adding 1 mL mESC base medium and pipette to dissociate colonies, transfer to a 15 mL Falcon tube, centrifuge 200 × g for 5 min, aspirate gelatin from the plate, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL mESC medium, plate an appropriate volume to achieve a 1:10–1:15 split ratio, top up to 1 mL with mESC medium and incubate.

steps.title: Coat ibidi plate with Matrigel
steps.instruction: Using cold tips, dispense 40–50 µL ice‑cold 100 % Matrigel into each well of an μ‑Slide 8‑well plate, avoid bubbles, and incubate 7–10 min at 37 °C to allow solidification.

steps.title: Add DMEM/F12 overlay
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL DMEM F12 to each Matrigel‑coated well to prevent the Matrigel from overdrying before cell plating.

steps.title: Dissociate 3D EpiSCs
steps.instruction: Wash the 3D EpiSC pellet with wash buffer, centrifuge (speed not specified), discard the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 1 mL N2B27.

steps.title: Plate 3D EpiSCs on Matrigel
steps.instruction: Remove the DMEM/F12 overlay, add 250 µL of the cell suspension to each well (≈1:4 ratio; ratio may vary 1:4–1:8), and incubate 10–15 min at 37 °C to allow attachment.

steps.title: Prepare 3D FAXN medium with Matrigel
steps.instruction: Dilute Matrigel to a final concentration of 5 % (v/v) in cold 3D FAXN medium using cold tips, then keep the mixture at 20–25 °C.

steps.title: Overlay cells with 3D FAXN medium
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the previous overlay and add 250 µL of the 5 % Matrigel‑containing 3D FAXN medium to each well, dispensing close to the wall to avoid detaching the cells.

steps.title: Fix cells with PFA
steps.instruction: Add 4 % paraformaldehyde to each well and incubate 20 min at 20–25 °C in the dark.

steps.title: Wash with PBS‑Tween
steps.instruction: Wash the wells three times with PBS containing 0.1 % Tween.

steps.title: Permeabilize cells
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL permeabilization buffer per well and incubate 30 min at 20–25 °C.

steps.title: Wash after permeabilization
steps.instruction: Wash the wells once with PBS 0.1 % Tween.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Add 150 µL of primary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer to each well and incubate 24 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash after primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Wash the wells three times with PBS 0.1 % Tween.

steps.title: Secondary antibody with DAPI
steps.instruction: Add 150 µL of secondary antibodies with DAPI diluted in blocking buffer to each well and incubate 2 h at 20–25 °C.

steps.title: Final washes and imaging
steps.instruction: Wash the wells three times with PBS 0.1 % Tween; samples are now ready for confocal microscopy.

description: The protocol below describes the specific steps for generating 3D Epiblast Stem Cells (3D EpiSCs) starting from mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs) and mouse epiblasts at embryonic day E5.5. Although we are not describing this here, EpiSCs can also be used as a starting point to generate 3D EpiSCs, following the same steps described for mESCs, as previously reported in.1 Our 3D culture is a self-renewing system of 3D EpiSCs that allows genetic manipulations that would be technically challenging in vivo.
